builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off
summary: The technique modifies standard LoRA training by adding a differentiable Rényi-2 effective-rank regularizer to the language-modeling loss, replacing the usual practice of relying on unpenalized low-rank updates that often underuse their configured rank. It costs additional training-time regularization and hyperparameter tuning, with the paper reporting that mean training perplexity improves or increases by at most 0.02 in all but one model-rank comparison, but it does not establish a serving-time advantage. It can fail if the workload is single-task, if the chosen λ or rank does not match the domain mix, or if the capacity gain does not translate into better downstream retention outside the tested settings.
rationale: It is potentially useful for constrained fine-tuning because it is compatible with LoRA-based parameter-efficient training, but its benefit is workload-sensitive enough to require validation before adoption.

claims.statement: The technique modifies standard LoRA training by adding a differentiable Rényi-2 effective-rank regularizer to the language-modeling loss, replacing the usual practice of relying on unpenalized low-rank updates that often underuse their configured rank. It costs additional training-time regularization and hyperparameter tuning, with the paper reporting that mean training perplexity improves or increases by at most 0.02 in all but one model-rank comparison, but it does not establish a serving-time advantage. It can fail if the workload is single-task, if the chosen λ or rank does not match the domain mix, or if the capacity gain does not translate into better downstream retention outside the tested settings.

The method lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least 16 in mixed-domain rank sweeps on three models, with a penalty weight of λ=0.01, relative to unpenalized LoRA; the abstract provides perplexity differences but not a multiplicative quality factor.
